content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (LOL-CAP).**

Section 21 is structurally strong — the cap is mutual, consequential damages are mutually excluded, and 21.3 carves out confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, with Customer's payment obligations expressly outside the cap. All of that meets the preferred position.

The failure is the cap quantum: 21.1 keys off "Fees", which §1.5 defines as the Implementation Fee and §1.8 fixes as a one-time USD 12,000 charge in the first Order Form — and 21.1 further narrows to "the first Order Form". The result is an effectively USD 12,000 cap irrespective of subscription spend, below even six months' fees and squarely in walk-away territory.

Redline (validated ok:true) makes the minimal change to 21.1 only: cap becomes the greater of all amounts paid or payable under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the preceding twelve months, or USD 1,000,000, with a stated fallback of a straight 12-month fees cap across all Order Forms.
